title: Mohd. Shahab v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
coram: Attau Rahman Masoodi, J.; Om Prakash Shukla, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; clause 6.5(b) representation left open with stay
headnote: Regular bills had been paid, but a further demand was raised for a mistake in those bills without prior intimation of the reason for rectification. The writ was disposed of without deciding the demand. The consumer may represent under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within two weeks; the competent authority must decide after opportunity, preferably within one month. Coercive measures are stayed for one month or until that decision.
facts: The petitioner, Mohd. Shahab, approached the Allahabad High Court at Lucknow against the State of Uttar Pradesh and the electricity authorities. Opposite parties 2 to 4 had raised a demand said to arise from a mistake in bills already issued. He had paid the regular electricity bills throughout. He disputed the further liability because he had not been informed of any reason before those bills were rectified.

holding_units.topic: Disputed rectification demand left to a clause 6.5(b) representation
holding_units.holding: Where regular electricity bills have been paid and the consumer disputes a further demand raised on account of a mistake in those bills, without prior intimation of the reason for rectification, the writ is disposed of by leaving him to a representation before the competent authority under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. If made within two weeks, the authority must decide it after due opportunity, expeditiously and preferably within one month of filing, and coercive measures are not to be taken for one month or until that decision.

principle_tags.application: The billing dispute was not adjudicated in writ. The petition was disposed of with liberty to represent to the competent authority under clause 6.5(b) within two weeks.
A further demand said to arise from mistaken bills, disputed for want of prior intimation of the reason for rectification, was left to the clause 6.5(b) representation.
Coercive measures against the consumer were directed not to be taken for one month or until decision on the clause 6.5(b) representation.

not_decided.point: Whether the demand raised on rectification of the bills was lawful, and whether prior intimation of the reason was required
not_decided.note: Left to the competent authority if a representation under clause 6.5(b) is made within two weeks
